definitions.displayName: Appendiceal NET staging and regional surgery
definitions.presentation: {patientName}, a 41-year-old man, attends the clinic after appendectomy identified a 2.6-cm well-differentiated grade-1 neuroendocrine tumor. The base margin is clear. Staging CT describes two small liver lesions that remain indeterminate on its acquired phases. The chest has no suspicious lesion. He is fit for further surgery.

nodes.displayName: Functional staging of a well-differentiated appendiceal NET
nodes.learningObjective: Combine well-differentiated NET biology and indeterminate cross-sectional staging to select receptor-targeted functional imaging.
nodes.stem: Which functional imaging study should next complete {patientName}'s appendiceal tumor staging?

choices.label: 18F-FDG PET/CT
choices.rationale: The supplied tumor is well differentiated. Current ASCRS guidance favors somatostatin-receptor PET/CT over FDG PET/CT for detecting disease in this setting.
choices.temptation: Apply a general metabolically active cancer-staging strategy to every appendiceal malignancy.
choices.counterfactual: A different, poorly differentiated or high-grade cancer biology can create an FDG-staging question. Exact use in that setting needs its own supported item.

choices.label: 68Ga-DOTATATE PET/CT
choices.rationale: The well-differentiated NET and unresolved possible metastatic lesions create a receptor-imaging indication. Ga-DOTA PET/CT can add staging information and has higher sensitivity than older receptor scintigraphy.
choices.temptation: Match receptor-targeted imaging to the tumor biology and residual staging question.
choices.counterfactual: A documented service limitation preventing receptor PET/CT can make the older somatostatin-receptor scintigraphy pathway an alternative after specialist review.

choices.label: 111In-pentetreotide scintigraphy
choices.rationale: Older somatostatin-receptor scintigraphy targets a relevant pathway but has largely been replaced by more sensitive Ga-DOTA PET/CT when the latter is available.
choices.temptation: Choose the familiar older receptor study without comparing its current role with PET-based receptor imaging.
choices.counterfactual: Receptor PET/CT unavailability could support specialist use of the older receptor study. That resource-constrained ranking is outside the present unconstrained comparison.

nodes.explanation: The lesion is a well-differentiated NET and the CT leaves possible metastatic disease unresolved. Somatostatin-receptor PET/CT can clarify staging in this situation. ASCRS describes Ga-DOTA PET/CT as more sensitive than older receptor scintigraphy for well-differentiated NET assessment.
nodes.identityReason: New staging objective distinct from the subsequent resection-extent decision.

reasoning.interpret: Identify well-differentiated NET biology and distinguish an indeterminate liver result from either established metastasis or adequate negative staging.
reasoning.apply: Choose the current receptor-targeted functional imaging method to resolve the staging question.
reasoning.closestError: Choose FDG PET/CT because the patient has cancer, or choose older receptor scintigraphy without comparing its current role.
reasoning.decidingObservation: Grade-1 well-differentiated NET with possible liver involvement unresolved by the acquired CT phases.
reasoning.consequence: The residual metastatic question can be staged with a less appropriate functional technique before further surgery.
reasoning.deletionTest: Grade and differentiation determine the biologic target. Indeterminate liver lesions establish the need for additional staging. Tumor size keeps the case inside the guideline's explicit higher-risk imaging scope. Clear base margin preserves a competing assumption of completed local surgery.
reasoning.counterfactual: Make receptor PET/CT unavailable while preserving the well-differentiated tumor and staging uncertainty. Older somatostatin-receptor scintigraphy becomes the relevant offered alternative after specialist review.
reasoning.cueAttack: All three options are functional nuclear studies with complete test estimates. The task says functional imaging without naming a receptor. The key is neither longest nor the sole specific modality. The grade and unresolved liver findings earn the inference.
reasoning.stageCategory: Functional staging study after cross-sectional imaging.
reasoning.difficulty: Predicted moderate for PGY-2/3 from confusing generic FDG staging with receptor-targeted NET staging and comparing current with older receptor imaging.
reasoning.oneBestAnswer: In the ordinary available-modality comparison, Ga-DOTA PET/CT best matches well-differentiated NET staging. The resource counterfactual changes that comparison explicitly.
reasoning.sequenceCheck: First node has no receptor study result or surgical recommendation in the visible context. Its feedback avoids the right-colectomy size rule tested later.
reasoning.repairRecord: Removed a generic PET-versus-no-imaging choice. Used three real functional studies, retained the actual CT uncertainty and removed a pre-answer receptor-availability sentence.

nodes.displayName: Regional surgery after a large appendiceal NET
nodes.learningObjective: Distinguish clear local margins from regional oncologic adequacy after staging a large appendiceal NET.
nodes.currentUpdate: At later follow-up, {patientName}'s completed liver characterization shows simple cysts, and the multidisciplinary staging review finds no distant disease. The permanent appendix specimen confirms a 2.6-cm well-differentiated NET with a clear base margin. The appendectomy included the mesoappendix, and he remains fit for surgery.
nodes.stem: Which further surgical plan should be recommended for {patientName}'s localized 2.6-cm appendiceal NET?

choices.label: Complete surgical treatment with the appendectomy
choices.rationale: A clear local margin and mesoappendix removal establish the appendectomy field. The tumor exceeds the directly supported 2-cm size boundary for recommending regional right hemicolectomy.
choices.temptation: Equate a margin-negative appendectomy with adequate regional treatment regardless of tumor size.
choices.counterfactual: A completely removed subcentimeter NET without unfavorable features can be adequately treated by appendectomy including the mesoappendix.

choices.label: Re-excise the appendiceal base with a cecal cuff
choices.rationale: A cecal cuff addresses local clearance. This tumor has a clear base margin, while its size makes the regional nodal field consequential.
choices.temptation: Treat completion surgery as a wider local-margin operation.
choices.counterfactual: A different localized lesion involving the base could call for a cecal cuff to obtain initial gross clearance. A margin-positive appendiceal NET requires its own oncologic review.

choices.label: Perform right hemicolectomy with regional nodes
choices.rationale: For a fit patient with a nonmetastatic appendiceal NET larger than 2 cm, ASCRS guidance supports right hemicolectomy to address the regional nodal basin despite the clear appendectomy margin.
choices.temptation: Apply the size and stage evidence to the regional surgical field.
choices.counterfactual: A completely excised subcentimeter favorable NET would favor ending surgical resection after appendectomy.

nodes.explanation: Completed staging establishes a localized surgical problem. The clear base margin addresses local clearance, while the 2.6-cm tumor exceeds the ASCRS greater-than-2-cm boundary for right hemicolectomy with regional nodal assessment.
nodes.identityReason: New regional-resection objective. The separate functional-staging concept retains its own identity and scheduling history.

reasoning.interpret: Read completed staging as localized disease and a clear base margin as evidence about the local appendectomy field.
reasoning.apply: Apply the directly sourced greater-than-2-cm boundary to the regional nodal operation.
reasoning.closestError: End surgery because the base margin is clear and the mesoappendix was included.
reasoning.decidingObservation: A confirmed 2.6-cm NET with no distant disease in a fit patient.
reasoning.consequence: The regional nodal basin receives neither the recommended resection nor its staging assessment.
reasoning.deletionTest: Without completed staging, the definitive treatment field remains unresolved. Without tumor size, the recommendation enters the controversial intermediate range. The clear margin and mesoappendix record make completed appendectomy a credible competing plan.
reasoning.counterfactual: Change the primary to a completely removed 0.7-cm well-differentiated NET with no unfavorable features. Completed appendectomy becomes the best offered surgical plan.
reasoning.cueAttack: Three specific surgical extents are compared. The question supplies the known diagnosis because operative extent is scored. No option is a generic discussion plan. The key has comparable length and no unique caution language. Clinical size recall remains part of the inference.
reasoning.stageCategory: Regional surgical extent after permanent pathology and completed staging.
reasoning.difficulty: Predicted moderate for PGY-2/3 from confusing local clearance with regional oncologic adequacy. Independent review should scrutinize whether the size rule is sufficiently discriminating.
reasoning.oneBestAnswer: The directly supported size boundary and localized staging support right hemicolectomy. The intermediate-size controversy is outside the supplied measurements.
reasoning.sequenceCheck: The preceding functional-imaging feedback discusses receptor staging only. This update supplies the actual completed staging result needed to choose the operative field.
reasoning.repairRecord: Replaced a size-threshold label question with a local-versus-regional completion plan. Kept the exact sourced boundary and added the completed local-field record for the closest error.

definitions.presentation: {patientName}, a 35-year-old woman, returns to the clinic after laparoscopic appendectomy for a perforated appendix. She initially resumed eating, then developed fever, deep pelvic pain and abdominal distension. She is passing stool. The port incisions are dry, the abdomen is tender without diffuse rigidity, and her circulation is stable. Pregnancy testing is negative, renal function is within its reporting interval and no prior iodinated-contrast reaction is recorded.

nodes.displayName: Investigation after post-appendectomy deterioration
nodes.learningObjective: Use a renewed postoperative inflammatory course and symptom depth to select imaging that maps a possible intra-abdominal source.
nodes.stem: Which investigation should the acute-care team obtain next for {patientName}'s renewed symptoms after appendectomy?

choices.label: Targeted ultrasound of the abdominal port sites
choices.rationale: A focused superficial study could assess a localized port-site collection. The represented fever and deep pelvic symptoms require examination of the intra-abdominal field.
choices.temptation: Attribute postoperative infection to the incision and choose the most accessible target.
choices.counterfactual: A focal swollen erythematous port-site mass with otherwise reassuring recovery could make a targeted superficial study appropriate.

choices.label: Contrast-enhanced abdominal and pelvic CT
choices.rationale: The recovery-then-deterioration pattern raises a deep intra-abdominal source question. Intravenous contrast-enhanced CT maps collections and their relation to bowel for subsequent source-control planning.
choices.temptation: Map the deep postoperative field after integrating trajectory, fever and pelvic localization.
choices.counterfactual: An isolated superficial port-site mass with a reassuring abdominal course would shift the target to port-site imaging.

choices.label: Upright and supine abdominal radiographs
choices.rationale: Radiographs can depict a bowel-gas pattern but provide limited characterization of an intra-abdominal infectious source. The renewed fever and deep pain make source mapping consequential.
choices.temptation: Treat the distension as a bowel-gas question while underweighting the inflammatory trajectory.
choices.counterfactual: A distinct supported bowel-obstruction or foreign-body question could call for radiographs. The present source-control investigation has a different target.

nodes.explanation: The return of fever and deep pelvic pain after initial recovery raises concern for a postoperative intra-abdominal source. CT with intravenous contrast maps the source and the anatomy needed for a treatment plan. A focused port study and plain films examine narrower targets.
nodes.identityReason: New postoperative source-localization objective, distinct from the legacy initial adult appendicitis modality decision.

reasoning.interpret: Read renewed fever after initial recovery and deep pelvic symptoms as a source-localization problem despite distension and reassuring incisions.
reasoning.apply: Choose contrast-enhanced cross-sectional assessment of the entire relevant postoperative field.
reasoning.closestError: Request abdominal radiographs for distension and assume the rest of the postoperative course is expected ileus.
reasoning.decidingObservation: New fever and deep pelvic pain after eating had resumed.
reasoning.consequence: A deep collection or ongoing source remains uncharacterized and source control is delayed.
reasoning.deletionTest: Recovery followed by deterioration changes the interpretation of distension. Symptom depth and incision observations distinguish the imaging target. Stability, pregnancy status and contrast history delimit this CT comparison.
reasoning.counterfactual: Replace the deep inflammatory course with an isolated tender erythematous port-site mass and otherwise reassuring abdominal recovery. Targeted port-site ultrasound becomes the appropriate offered investigation.
reasoning.cueAttack: All three choices are real investigations and carry test estimates. The task avoids naming an abscess or CT. The negative incision observation localizes the clinical question, while the distension provides the credible radiograph temptation. The key is shorter than the port-site option.
reasoning.stageCategory: Current investigation of renewed postoperative symptoms.
reasoning.difficulty: Predicted moderate for PGY-2/3 from mistaking the renewed inflammatory course for uncomplicated ileus or a superficial wound problem.
reasoning.oneBestAnswer: Stable physiology permits cross-sectional localization, and the represented deep inflammatory problem calls for abdominal and pelvic source mapping.
reasoning.sequenceCheck: First node includes no collection measurement, drainage route or antibiotic endpoint. Those findings are revealed only in later updates.
reasoning.repairRecord: Replaced an abscess-diagnosis giveaway with a trajectory-and-target imaging task. Removed a sentence announcing the missing CT and supplied contrast-related context without a numeric cutoff.

nodes.displayName: Source control of a localized post-appendectomy collection
nodes.learningObjective: Interpret localized anatomy and treatment response to choose a source-control route after appendectomy.
nodes.currentUpdate: The receiving hospital's CT shows a 5.5-cm rim-enhancing pelvic collection containing gas. It abuts the bladder and rectum, with a posterior catheter path clear of bowel. No enteric contrast leak or diffuse intraperitoneal fluid is seen. Fever and focal pain persist after intravenous antibiotics. {patientName} remains alert with stable blood pressure and no diffuse rigidity.
nodes.stem: Which source-control plan should be recommended now for {patientName}'s postoperative pelvic collection?

choices.label: Continue intravenous antibiotics with serial examination
choices.rationale: Antibiotics can suffice for selected small or resolving collections. Persistent infection with this organized accessible collection supports evacuation as part of source control.
choices.temptation: Treat stable physiology as evidence that antimicrobial treatment has controlled the source.
choices.counterfactual: A small collection shrinking with complete clinical improvement and no safe access route could support continued medical management.

choices.label: Perform operative exploration with pelvic drainage
choices.rationale: Exploration can control generalized contamination, an ongoing enteric leak or a collection inaccessible to percutaneous treatment. The supplied single localized collection has a safe catheter route and stable physiology.
choices.temptation: Treat every postoperative gas-containing collection as a failure requiring a return to the operating room.
choices.counterfactual: Diffuse rigidity and active enteric leakage would favor prompt operative source control.

choices.label: Perform image-guided pelvic catheter drainage
choices.rationale: Persistent infection and an organized localized collection call for source control. The safe posterior route and absence of generalized peritonitis support image-guided catheter drainage with ongoing antimicrobial care.
choices.temptation: Use the represented anatomic access and physiologic state to select a less invasive source-control route.
choices.counterfactual: A demonstrated ongoing bowel leak with generalized peritonitis would shift treatment to operative control of contamination.

nodes.explanation: The organized collection and persistent fever indicate a residual source needing control. Stable physiology, localization and a safe catheter route support image-guided drainage with antimicrobial therapy. Generalized contamination or an uncontrolled enteric leak would change the source-control operation.
nodes.identityReason: New postoperative treatment-route objective. It is separate from disputed initial treatment of a primary appendiceal phlegmon or abscess.

reasoning.interpret: Integrate an organized gas-containing collection and persistent symptoms as incomplete source control, then assess localization and the actual catheter path.
reasoning.apply: Choose image-guided drainage for the accessible localized source while continuing shared antimicrobial care.
reasoning.closestError: Continue antibiotics because the patient is stable, or operate because postoperative gas is interpreted as proof of uncontrolled bowel leakage.
reasoning.decidingObservation: Persistent infection, a single organized collection with a bowel-free catheter route and no represented ongoing leak or generalized peritonitis.
reasoning.consequence: Delayed source control or an unnecessarily invasive operation.
reasoning.deletionTest: Deleting persistent symptoms makes continued medical care more plausible. Deleting route anatomy makes the drainage recommendation underspecified. Generalized-peritonitis and leak observations constrain the choice against operative source control. The 5.5-cm value is a constructed case observation and supplies no universal drainage cutoff.
reasoning.counterfactual: Add diffuse rigidity and active enteric leakage on CT. Operative exploration with control of the leak becomes the best offered source-control plan.
reasoning.cueAttack: All three options are concrete source-control policies. The key has intermediate length. The catheter path is necessary procedural anatomy, and is described without saying the procedure is available or will avoid delay. Every offered test/procedural choice has an explicit timing classification.
reasoning.stageCategory: Source-control route after cross-sectional anatomy and observed antibiotic response.
reasoning.difficulty: Predicted moderate to hard for PGY-2/3 from balancing persistent infection against stability, postoperative gas and actual source-control access.
reasoning.oneBestAnswer: For this localized accessible collection with persistent illness, catheter drainage is the favored proposed route. There is no claimed size-only rule or universal rank across all postoperative abscesses.
reasoning.sequenceCheck: The prior node explains source localization only. It supplies neither the drain route nor a general percutaneous-drainage recommendation. This update adds the decisive anatomy and response.
reasoning.repairRecord: Removed a sentence declaring the collection drainable and replaced it with the posterior path anatomy. Re-solved the operative-leak and resolving-collection counterfactuals.

nodes.displayName: Antibiotic endpoint after source control and recovery
nodes.learningObjective: Interpret clinical recovery after adequate drainage when an inflammatory laboratory value remains mildly abnormal.
nodes.currentUpdate: At later clinic review, catheter drainage has evacuated the collection, and the treating team has documented source control without ongoing bowel leakage. {patientName} has completed four days of an active antibiotic course after drainage. She is afebrile, eating, walking and free of abdominal pain. Her leukocyte count has fallen substantially and remains slightly above the laboratory reference interval. She is immunocompetent.
nodes.stem: Which antibiotic plan should be recommended now for {patientName} after this completed course and source control?

choices.label: Continue treatment until the leukocyte count normalizes
choices.rationale: Waiting for every inflammatory laboratory value to normalize can prolong therapy after adequate source control and clinical recovery. Fixed short-course evidence supports ending the completed course in this represented patient.
choices.temptation: Use a mildly abnormal leukocyte count as proof of ongoing infection despite recovery.
choices.counterfactual: Renewed fever, pain or organ dysfunction would require a fresh source-control assessment and a supported active-treatment plan.

choices.label: End antibiotic treatment after the completed course
choices.rationale: Adequate source control and complete clinical recovery support ending the completed short course. An isolated falling mildly elevated leukocyte count does not establish a need for extension.
choices.temptation: Integrate source control, completed active therapy and the actual recovery trajectory.
choices.counterfactual: Persistent fever or recurrent abdominal findings would change the decision to renewed source assessment and active infection treatment.

choices.label: Continue treatment pending repeat abdominal and pelvic CT
choices.rationale: Clinical recovery after adequate drainage supports ending the completed course. New or persistent illness would establish a separate indication for CT assessment of residual infection while treatment is reassessed.
choices.temptation: Require another source-imaging assessment despite documented source control and clinical recovery.
choices.counterfactual: Recurrent deep pain and fever would support CT assessment for a residual or new source while therapy is reassessed.

nodes.explanation: The relevant endpoint combines adequate source control, a completed active short course and clinical recovery. The fixed-course evidence does not require normalization of every inflammatory value. A recurrence of illness would trigger reassessment of the source and treatment plan.
nodes.identityReason: New source-control-and-response endpoint objective. It does not install a fixed duration in diagnostic wait metadata or author a minimum appendicitis antibiotic duration.

reasoning.interpret: Separate a falling mildly abnormal leukocyte count from clinical evidence of persistent infection after adequate drainage.
reasoning.apply: End the completed active course instead of extending to a laboratory or radiographic endpoint.
reasoning.closestError: Continue antibiotics until the leukocyte count enters the laboratory reference interval.
reasoning.decidingObservation: Adequate source control, completed active treatment and afebrile pain-free functional recovery.
reasoning.consequence: Unnecessary antimicrobial exposure and investigation.
reasoning.deletionTest: Deleting source-control adequacy or clinical recovery invalidates the stop recommendation. The mildly abnormal falling count creates the closest competing endpoint. Four days is the constructed completed course with direct support from Global Alliance statement 8, not a newly authored mandatory minimum.
reasoning.counterfactual: Replace recovery with renewed deep pain and fever. Continuing active treatment while obtaining CT to assess a residual source becomes the best offered plan, with duration determined after reassessment.
reasoning.cueAttack: All labels specify antibiotic endpoints. The key and alternatives have comparable length. Every CT-containing plan has a CT estimate. No specific regimen is chosen because the active regimen is common background care. Removed a negative-culture result that would have provided an extra stopping cue.
reasoning.stageCategory: Antibiotic management after a completed active course and documented source control.
reasoning.difficulty: Predicted moderate for PGY-2/3 from treating incomplete laboratory normalization as treatment failure despite source control and recovery.
reasoning.oneBestAnswer: The represented completed-course scenario fits fixed short-course evidence. Minimum duration, resistant pathogens, immunosuppression and unresolved source-control scenarios require separate decisions.
reasoning.sequenceCheck: Prior feedback establishes the reason for drainage, while this node adds actual evacuation, clinical response and a completed antibiotic course. Earlier feedback states no antibiotic endpoint or duration.
reasoning.repairRecord: Replaced a duration-recall question with a source-control-and-recovery endpoint. Removed a new drug regimen and retained the observed completed course. The counterfactual was re-solved for recurrent illness.

questions.stem: Which hospital evaluation should be recommended now for {patientName}'s worsening right-sided abdominal findings?

answerChoices.label: Repeat contrast-enhanced abdominal and pelvic CT

answerChoices.distractorRationale: A repeat scan can help when the original acquisition was inadequate or a new localization problem develops. Here, adequate imaging has been followed by a progressively abnormal serial examination, supporting exploration.

answerChoices.distractorRationale: Observation was a reasonable response to the initial negative scan. The newly progressive focal findings change the balance toward exploration.

answerChoices.distractorRationale: Right hemicolectomy fits an established invasive localized carcinoma. This record supplies a suspicious localized appendix lesion with a free base and definitive histology pending.

questions.stem: Which treatment referral should be recommended now for {patientName}'s appendiceal mucinous disease?

cases.presentation: {patientName}, a 35-year-old woman, returns to the clinic after laparoscopic appendectomy for a perforated appendix. She initially resumed eating, then developed fever, deep pelvic pain and abdominal distension. She is passing stool. The port incisions are dry, the abdomen is tender without diffuse rigidity, and her circulation is stable. Pregnancy testing is negative, renal function is within its reporting interval and no prior iodinated-contrast reaction is recorded.

decisionNodes.stem: Which investigation should the acute-care team obtain next for {patientName}'s renewed symptoms after appendectomy?

answerChoices.label: Targeted ultrasound of the abdominal port sites
answerChoices.rationale: A focused superficial study could assess a localized port-site collection. The represented fever and deep pelvic symptoms require examination of the intra-abdominal field.

answerChoices.label: Contrast-enhanced abdominal and pelvic CT
answerChoices.rationale: The recovery-then-deterioration pattern raises a deep intra-abdominal source question. Intravenous contrast-enhanced CT maps collections and their relation to bowel for subsequent source-control planning.

answerChoices.label: Upright and supine abdominal radiographs
answerChoices.rationale: Radiographs can depict a bowel-gas pattern but provide limited characterization of an intra-abdominal infectious source. The renewed fever and deep pain make source mapping consequential.

decisionNodes.explanation: The return of fever and deep pelvic pain after initial recovery raises concern for a postoperative intra-abdominal source. CT with intravenous contrast maps the source and the anatomy needed for a treatment plan. A focused port study and plain films examine narrower targets.

decisionNodes.currentUpdate: The receiving hospital's CT shows a 5.5-cm rim-enhancing pelvic collection containing gas. It abuts the bladder and rectum, with a posterior catheter path clear of bowel. No enteric contrast leak or diffuse intraperitoneal fluid is seen. Fever and focal pain persist after intravenous antibiotics. {patientName} remains alert with stable blood pressure and no diffuse rigidity.
decisionNodes.stem: Which source-control plan should be recommended now for {patientName}'s postoperative pelvic collection?

answerChoices.label: Continue intravenous antibiotics with serial examination
answerChoices.rationale: Antibiotics can suffice for selected small or resolving collections. Persistent infection with this organized accessible collection supports evacuation as part of source control.

answerChoices.label: Perform operative exploration with pelvic drainage
answerChoices.rationale: Exploration can control generalized contamination, an ongoing enteric leak or a collection inaccessible to percutaneous treatment. The supplied single localized collection has a safe catheter route and stable physiology.

answerChoices.label: Perform image-guided pelvic catheter drainage
answerChoices.rationale: Persistent infection and an organized localized collection call for source control. The safe posterior route and absence of generalized peritonitis support image-guided catheter drainage with ongoing antimicrobial care.

decisionNodes.explanation: The organized collection and persistent fever indicate a residual source needing control. Stable physiology, localization and a safe catheter route support image-guided drainage with antimicrobial therapy. Generalized contamination or an uncontrolled enteric leak would change the source-control operation.
sourceLabels: Diagnosis and treatment of acute appendicitis, 2020 WSES update

decisionNodes.currentUpdate: At later clinic review, catheter drainage has evacuated the collection, and the treating team has documented source control without ongoing bowel leakage. {patientName} has completed four days of an active antibiotic course after drainage. She is afebrile, eating, walking and free of abdominal pain. Her leukocyte count has fallen substantially and remains slightly above the laboratory reference interval. She is immunocompetent.
decisionNodes.stem: Which antibiotic plan should be recommended now for {patientName} after this completed course and source control?

answerChoices.label: Continue treatment until the leukocyte count normalizes
answerChoices.rationale: Waiting for every inflammatory laboratory value to normalize can prolong therapy after adequate source control and clinical recovery. Fixed short-course evidence supports ending the completed course in this represented patient.

answerChoices.label: End antibiotic treatment after the completed course
answerChoices.rationale: Adequate source control and complete clinical recovery support ending the completed short course. An isolated falling mildly elevated leukocyte count does not establish a need for extension.

answerChoices.label: Continue treatment pending repeat abdominal and pelvic CT
answerChoices.rationale: Clinical recovery after adequate drainage supports ending the completed course. New or persistent illness would establish a separate indication for CT assessment of residual infection while treatment is reassessed.

decisionNodes.explanation: The relevant endpoint combines adequate source control, a completed active short course and clinical recovery. The fixed-course evidence does not require normalization of every inflammatory value. A recurrence of illness would trigger reassessment of the source and treatment plan.

authoringConcepts.displayName: Progressive symptoms after negative imaging
authoringConcepts.learningObjective: Integrate adequate negative imaging with a worsening serial examination to choose further operative evaluation.
authoringConcepts.identityReason: The returned B2B14 task selected a CT protocol. This version scores escalation after adequate negative imaging and clinical progression. It requires a new concept identity and preserves the older protocol construct and history.

authoringConcepts.displayName: Completion surgery after invasive appendiceal pathology
authoringConcepts.learningObjective: Use invasive histology and completed staging to select nodal-basin resection after a margin-negative appendectomy.
authoringConcepts.identityReason: New gap objective. The two legacy live concepts concern imaging and antibiotics-versus-operation selection, and contain no postoperative cancer-resection objective.

authoringConcepts.displayName: Colonic evaluation after an appendiceal abscess
authoringConcepts.learningObjective: Recognize a post-abscess neoplasm concern and select colonic evaluation before formal resection planning.
authoringConcepts.identityReason: New gap objective after nonoperative treatment of complicated appendicitis.

authoringConcepts.displayName: Persistent appendiceal abnormality after abscess recovery
authoringConcepts.learningObjective: Integrate a normal colonic lumen with persistent appendiceal imaging findings to choose interval tissue evaluation.
authoringConcepts.identityReason: New gap objective. The held general younger-adult interval policy remains separate from this older patient with persistent suspicious imaging.

authoringConcepts.displayName: Initial extent for an unruptured appendiceal lesion
authoringConcepts.learningObjective: Use the base anatomy and uncertain final tumor type to select intact limited resection before definitive oncologic pathology.
authoringConcepts.identityReason: New anatomy-to-operative-extent objective in the assigned appendiceal-lesion scope.

authoringConcepts.displayName: Microscopic margin after complete nonperforated LAMN resection
authoringConcepts.learningObjective: Interpret microscopic margin involvement within an otherwise completely resected nonperforated LAMN before recommending additional bowel resection.
authoringConcepts.identityReason: New pathology-and-clearance objective. It must retain a separate identity from invasive adenocarcinoma completion colectomy.

authoringConcepts.displayName: Treatment field for appendiceal mucinous peritoneal disease
authoringConcepts.learningObjective: Integrate cellular peritoneal pathology and disease distribution to choose the appropriate oncologic treatment service.
authoringConcepts.identityReason: New treatment-field objective. It is separate from local LAMN margin management and regional invasive-cancer resection.

authoringConcepts.displayName: Resection after goblet cell adenocarcinoma
authoringConcepts.learningObjective: Reconcile a historical carcinoid label with definitive goblet cell adenocarcinoma pathology when selecting completion surgery.
authoringConcepts.identityReason: New histologic-identity-to-treatment objective. It preserves a distinct construct from well-differentiated appendiceal NET size decisions.

authoringConcepts.displayName: Functional staging of a well-differentiated appendiceal NET
authoringConcepts.learningObjective: Combine well-differentiated NET biology and indeterminate cross-sectional staging to select receptor-targeted functional imaging.
authoringConcepts.identityReason: New staging objective distinct from the subsequent resection-extent decision.

authoringConcepts.displayName: Regional surgery after a large appendiceal NET
authoringConcepts.learningObjective: Distinguish clear local margins from regional oncologic adequacy after staging a large appendiceal NET.
authoringConcepts.identityReason: New regional-resection objective. The separate functional-staging concept retains its own identity and scheduling history.

authoringConcepts.displayName: Investigation after post-appendectomy deterioration
authoringConcepts.learningObjective: Use a renewed postoperative inflammatory course and symptom depth to select imaging that maps a possible intra-abdominal source.
authoringConcepts.identityReason: New postoperative source-localization objective, distinct from the legacy initial adult appendicitis modality decision.

authoringConcepts.displayName: Source control of a localized post-appendectomy collection
authoringConcepts.learningObjective: Interpret localized anatomy and treatment response to choose a source-control route after appendectomy.
authoringConcepts.identityReason: New postoperative treatment-route objective. It is separate from disputed initial treatment of a primary appendiceal phlegmon or abscess.

authoringConcepts.displayName: Antibiotic endpoint after source control and recovery
authoringConcepts.learningObjective: Interpret clinical recovery after adequate drainage when an inflammatory laboratory value remains mildly abnormal.
authoringConcepts.identityReason: New source-control-and-response endpoint objective. It does not install a fixed duration in diagnostic wait metadata or author a minimum appendicitis antibiotic duration.

checks.interpret: Read the acquisition as adequate and the later guarding as genuine progression after an initially reasonable observation period.
checks.apply: Choose exploratory evaluation after the clinical course has outgrown reliance on the initial scan.
checks.closestError: Continue observation because the appendix was described as normal on CT.
checks.decidingObservation: New involuntary guarding and increasingly focal tenderness during observation.
checks.consequence: An evolving operative abdominal process remains untreated.
checks.deletionTest: The acquisition sentence distinguishes repeat imaging from exploration. Deleting the interval deterioration makes observation defensible. Pregnancy status and circulation delimit the acute pathway. Removed the classic migratory-pain and hematuria shortcuts from B2B14.
checks.counterfactual: Replace new guarding with steady pain resolution and a soft repeat examination. Continued hospital observation becomes the best offered plan.
checks.cueAttack: All offered actions are credible hospital evaluations and the key has intermediate length. The task asks for evaluation without naming exploration, missed appendicitis or a missing action. The necessary deterioration is clinical evidence. A prior scan and its adequacy preserve a real competing observation strategy.
checks.stageCategory: Current hospital evaluation after completed imaging and observation. Three concrete diagnostic strategies.
checks.difficulty: Predicted moderate for PGY-2/3. The intended error is over-reliance on an adequate negative CT when the serial examination changes. Independent review must judge the strength of this competition.
checks.oneBestAnswer: The documented worsening after observation distinguishes exploration from simply repeating the same adequate scan or extending the same observation strategy.
checks.sequenceCheck: First node has no earlier feedback or future pathology. Its explanation discusses the escalation decision and supplies no later oncologic operation.
checks.repairRecord: The protocol-matching draft was replaced by a new escalation construct. A second manual pass retained scan adequacy and clinical chronology, and removed an extra fever sentence that added no decision information.

distractorChecks.temptation: Treat the earlier scan as an imaging problem that another identical study will settle.
distractorChecks.rankingRationale: A repeat scan can help when the original acquisition was inadequate or a new localization problem develops. Here, adequate imaging has been followed by a progressively abnormal serial examination, supporting exploration.
distractorChecks.counterfactual: An incomplete outside acquisition with an unexamined symptomatic region would favor obtaining appropriate cross-sectional imaging before exploration.

distractorChecks.temptation: Give the reassuring CT more weight than the interval examination.
distractorChecks.rankingRationale: Observation was a reasonable response to the initial negative scan. The newly progressive focal findings change the balance toward exploration.
distractorChecks.counterfactual: A clearly improving examination without new guarding would support continued monitored observation.

checks.interpret: Distinguish destructive invasive pathology from noninfiltrative mucinous disease and interpret a clear base margin as a local result.
checks.apply: Use localized staging and invasive histology to select regional oncologic resection.
checks.closestError: Treat the margin-negative appendectomy as complete oncologic surgery.
checks.decidingObservation: Permanent whole-specimen invasive glands into mesoappendiceal fat, paired with absence of disseminated disease on completed staging.
checks.consequence: Regional nodal disease remains unstaged and the recommended oncologic field remains unresected.
checks.deletionTest: Deleting permanent invasive histology makes the correct extent indeterminate. Removing completed staging creates a competing disseminated-disease pathway. The clear margin earns its place by making limited local completion appear attractive.
checks.counterfactual: Replace infiltrative carcinoma with margin-negative nonperforated LAMN confined to the appendix. Completed appendectomy becomes sufficient surgical treatment.
checks.cueAttack: Three surgical-extent plans answer the same task. The key contains no unique qualifier about safety or discussion. A clear margin supplies a credible reason to stop, while the invasive pattern must change that conclusion.
checks.stageCategory: Definitive surgical extent after permanent pathology and staging.
checks.difficulty: Predicted moderate for PGY-2/3 from confusing local margin clearance with adequate oncologic regional surgery.
checks.oneBestAnswer: The fully characterized invasive localized tumor supports right hemicolectomy. The specimen has already supplied local-margin clearance.
checks.sequenceCheck: The first node explains escalation after imaging and never mentions a malignancy or colectomy. All pathology and staging appear only in this later update.
checks.repairRecord: Replaced an isolated histology-label question with a consequential completion-operation task. Re-solved after moving staging and whole-specimen provenance into the current update.

distractorChecks.temptation: Equate completion cancer surgery with taking a wider local margin.
distractorChecks.rankingRationale: A cecal cuff addresses local clearance. This specimen already has a clear base margin, while the invasive diagnosis creates a regional nodal question.
distractorChecks.counterfactual: An incidental lesion involving the appendiceal base without established invasive cancer could call for a limited cecal resection to obtain a grossly clear margin.

distractorChecks.temptation: Apply the limited-resection approach for localized low-grade mucinous neoplasia to an invasive carcinoma.
distractorChecks.rankingRationale: Clear appendectomy margins establish local removal. The invasive histology still supports regional nodal-basin resection in this fit patient with localized disease.
distractorChecks.counterfactual: A margin-negative, nonperforated LAMN confined to the appendix would make completed appendectomy sufficient surgical treatment.

checks.interpret: Separate resolution of infection from the persistent focal structural finding and the older patient's neoplasm concern.
checks.apply: Choose the preoperative investigation that examines potentially synchronous colonic disease.

checks.decidingObservation: Persistent appendiceal-cecal nodularity of uncertain origin after abscess resolution in a 62-year-old who has never had colonoscopy.
checks.consequence: A synchronous colonic lesion can be missed while an incomplete operative field is planned.
checks.deletionTest: The collapsed collection and resolved symptoms distinguish this workup from acute drainage. Nodularity of uncertain organ origin and the patient's age give the residual finding importance. Colonoscopy history establishes the acquisition need. Base anatomy remains obscured until the later reassessment.
checks.counterfactual: Replace symptom resolution with renewed fever and focal pain after drainage. Repeat CT to assess residual infection becomes the best offered investigation before elective colonic assessment.
checks.cueAttack: The task asks for an investigation without stating colon screening. All choices are named diagnostic procedures. The key is shorter than both distractors. The nodule gives biopsy a real temptation, while prior abscess resolution and age must be integrated.
checks.difficulty: Predicted moderate for PGY-2/3 from choosing tissue targeting or repeated abscess imaging before colonic evaluation. The counterfactual changes the actual clinical trajectory and re-ranks the offered CT.

distractorChecks.temptation: Seek a tumor label by the most direct apparent target before considering the adjacent colon.

distractorChecks.counterfactual: Renewed fever and focal pain after drainage would favor repeat CT to assess a residual infectious source before elective colonic workup.

distractorChecks.counterfactual: High-grade unresectable disease or solid-organ metastases could favor a systemic-treatment pathway after multidisciplinary assessment.

distractorChecks.temptation: Transfer the localized appendiceal-cancer completion operation to disseminated mucinous disease.
distractorChecks.rankingRationale: A right colectomy addresses a regional bowel and nodal field. The represented low-grade mucinous disease occupies multiple peritoneal regions, which require a peritoneal-surface treatment assessment.
distractorChecks.counterfactual: Nonmetastatic invasive appendiceal adenocarcinoma would support referral for oncologic right colectomy.

checks.interpret: Recognize an infiltrative goblet-cell epithelial tumor on the complete permanent specimen despite historical carcinoid terminology and focal neuroendocrine staining.
checks.apply: Choose the localized adenocarcinoma resection pathway despite the small size and clear local margin.
checks.closestError: Apply small-NET surgical rules because the original report used carcinoid.
checks.decidingObservation: Complete permanent sampling shows infiltrative mucin-filled goblet-cell clusters, with focal synaptophysin expression.
checks.consequence: A clinically distinct invasive epithelial cancer receives an inadequate regional surgical plan.
checks.deletionTest: Historical terminology, size and staining each establish the competing NET interpretation. Definitive review resolves it. Staging and fitness delimit the completion-operation recommendation. The clear margin distinguishes local from nodal completion.
checks.counterfactual: Replace expert review with a completely removed 0.7-cm grade-1 well-differentiated NET without unfavorable features. Complete treatment with appendectomy becomes the appropriate offered surgical plan.
checks.cueAttack: Three specific surgical-extent choices share the same task. The current report supplies morphology while withholding the updated tumor label, so the historical carcinoid wording requires reinterpretation. The key carries no unique counseling or caution qualifier.
checks.stageCategory: Completion surgical extent after definitive pathology and staging.
checks.difficulty: Predicted moderate to hard for PGY-2/3 because a familiar small-carcinoid rule competes with updated tumor identity.
checks.oneBestAnswer: The infiltrative goblet-cell epithelial morphology and localized stage favor the adenocarcinoma nodal-resection pathway.
checks.sequenceCheck: Standalone case. The learner has no earlier NET or colectomy explanation in the visible encounter.
checks.repairRecord: Removed an immunostain-only classification task. A second pass also removed the explicit updated diagnosis from the presentation, retaining complete permanent morphology and the concrete surgical consequence. Re-solved the small favorable NET counterfactual.

distractorChecks.temptation: Anchor on the old carcinoid label, small measured size and focal neuroendocrine stain.
distractorChecks.rankingRationale: A small favorable well-differentiated NET can have a limited surgical field. Expert review has established infiltrative goblet cell adenocarcinoma, which follows the adenocarcinoma pathway.
distractorChecks.counterfactual: A completely removed subcentimeter well-differentiated NET without unfavorable features would support completed appendectomy.

distractorChecks.temptation: Treat further surgery as a local-margin operation after a small appendiceal tumor.
distractorChecks.rankingRationale: The clear base margin already addresses local clearance. A cecal cuff would leave the regional nodal question created by the adenocarcinoma diagnosis unresolved.
distractorChecks.counterfactual: Gross localized base involvement of an unclassified appendiceal lesion could require limited cecal resection for clearance.

checks.interpret: Identify well-differentiated NET biology and distinguish an indeterminate liver result from either established metastasis or adequate negative staging.
checks.apply: Choose the current receptor-targeted functional imaging method to resolve the staging question.
checks.closestError: Choose FDG PET/CT because the patient has cancer, or choose older receptor scintigraphy without comparing its current role.
checks.decidingObservation: Grade-1 well-differentiated NET with possible liver involvement unresolved by the acquired CT phases.
checks.consequence: The residual metastatic question can be staged with a less appropriate functional technique before further surgery.
checks.deletionTest: Grade and differentiation determine the biologic target. Indeterminate liver lesions establish the need for additional staging. Tumor size keeps the case inside the guideline's explicit higher-risk imaging scope. Clear base margin preserves a competing assumption of completed local surgery.
checks.counterfactual: Make receptor PET/CT unavailable while preserving the well-differentiated tumor and staging uncertainty. Older somatostatin-receptor scintigraphy becomes the relevant offered alternative after specialist review.
checks.cueAttack: All three options are functional nuclear studies with complete test estimates. The task says functional imaging without naming a receptor. The key is neither longest nor the sole specific modality. The grade and unresolved liver findings earn the inference.
checks.stageCategory: Functional staging study after cross-sectional imaging.
checks.difficulty: Predicted moderate for PGY-2/3 from confusing generic FDG staging with receptor-targeted NET staging and comparing current with older receptor imaging.
checks.oneBestAnswer: In the ordinary available-modality comparison, Ga-DOTA PET/CT best matches well-differentiated NET staging. The resource counterfactual changes that comparison explicitly.
checks.sequenceCheck: First node has no receptor study result or surgical recommendation in the visible context. Its feedback avoids the right-colectomy size rule tested later.
checks.repairRecord: Removed a generic PET-versus-no-imaging choice. Used three real functional studies, retained the actual CT uncertainty and removed a pre-answer receptor-availability sentence.

distractorChecks.temptation: Apply a general metabolically active cancer-staging strategy to every appendiceal malignancy.
distractorChecks.rankingRationale: The supplied tumor is well differentiated. Current ASCRS guidance favors somatostatin-receptor PET/CT over FDG PET/CT for detecting disease in this setting.
distractorChecks.counterfactual: A different, poorly differentiated or high-grade cancer biology can create an FDG-staging question. Exact use in that setting needs its own supported item.

distractorChecks.temptation: Choose the familiar older receptor study without comparing its current role with PET-based receptor imaging.
distractorChecks.rankingRationale: Older somatostatin-receptor scintigraphy targets a relevant pathway but has largely been replaced by more sensitive Ga-DOTA PET/CT when the latter is available.
distractorChecks.counterfactual: Receptor PET/CT unavailability could support specialist use of the older receptor study. That resource-constrained ranking is outside the present unconstrained comparison.

checks.interpret: Read completed staging as localized disease and a clear base margin as evidence about the local appendectomy field.
checks.apply: Apply the directly sourced greater-than-2-cm boundary to the regional nodal operation.
checks.closestError: End surgery because the base margin is clear and the mesoappendix was included.
checks.decidingObservation: A confirmed 2.6-cm NET with no distant disease in a fit patient.
checks.consequence: The regional nodal basin receives neither the recommended resection nor its staging assessment.
checks.deletionTest: Without completed staging, the definitive treatment field remains unresolved. Without tumor size, the recommendation enters the controversial intermediate range. The clear margin and mesoappendix record make completed appendectomy a credible competing plan.
checks.counterfactual: Change the primary to a completely removed 0.7-cm well-differentiated NET with no unfavorable features. Completed appendectomy becomes the best offered surgical plan.
checks.cueAttack: Three specific surgical extents are compared. The question supplies the known diagnosis because operative extent is scored. No option is a generic discussion plan. The key has comparable length and no unique caution language. Clinical size recall remains part of the inference.
checks.stageCategory: Regional surgical extent after permanent pathology and completed staging.
checks.difficulty: Predicted moderate for PGY-2/3 from confusing local clearance with regional oncologic adequacy. Independent review should scrutinize whether the size rule is sufficiently discriminating.
checks.oneBestAnswer: The directly supported size boundary and localized staging support right hemicolectomy. The intermediate-size controversy is outside the supplied measurements.
checks.sequenceCheck: The preceding functional-imaging feedback discusses receptor staging only. This update supplies the actual completed staging result needed to choose the operative field.
checks.repairRecord: Replaced a size-threshold label question with a local-versus-regional completion plan. Kept the exact sourced boundary and added the completed local-field record for the closest error.

distractorChecks.temptation: Equate a margin-negative appendectomy with adequate regional treatment regardless of tumor size.
distractorChecks.rankingRationale: A clear local margin and mesoappendix removal establish the appendectomy field. The tumor exceeds the directly supported 2-cm size boundary for recommending regional right hemicolectomy.
distractorChecks.counterfactual: A completely removed subcentimeter NET without unfavorable features can be adequately treated by appendectomy including the mesoappendix.

distractorChecks.temptation: Treat completion surgery as a wider local-margin operation.
distractorChecks.rankingRationale: A cecal cuff addresses local clearance. This tumor has a clear base margin, while its size makes the regional nodal field consequential.
distractorChecks.counterfactual: A different localized lesion involving the base could call for a cecal cuff to obtain initial gross clearance. A margin-positive appendiceal NET requires its own oncologic review.

checks.interpret: Read renewed fever after initial recovery and deep pelvic symptoms as a source-localization problem despite distension and reassuring incisions.
checks.apply: Choose contrast-enhanced cross-sectional assessment of the entire relevant postoperative field.
checks.closestError: Request abdominal radiographs for distension and assume the rest of the postoperative course is expected ileus.
checks.decidingObservation: New fever and deep pelvic pain after eating had resumed.
checks.consequence: A deep collection or ongoing source remains uncharacterized and source control is delayed.
checks.deletionTest: Recovery followed by deterioration changes the interpretation of distension. Symptom depth and incision observations distinguish the imaging target. Stability, pregnancy status and contrast history delimit this CT comparison.
checks.counterfactual: Replace the deep inflammatory course with an isolated tender erythematous port-site mass and otherwise reassuring abdominal recovery. Targeted port-site ultrasound becomes the appropriate offered investigation.
checks.cueAttack: All three choices are real investigations and carry test estimates. The task avoids naming an abscess or CT. The negative incision observation localizes the clinical question, while the distension provides the credible radiograph temptation. The key is shorter than the port-site option.
checks.stageCategory: Current investigation of renewed postoperative symptoms.
checks.difficulty: Predicted moderate for PGY-2/3 from mistaking the renewed inflammatory course for uncomplicated ileus or a superficial wound problem.
checks.oneBestAnswer: Stable physiology permits cross-sectional localization, and the represented deep inflammatory problem calls for abdominal and pelvic source mapping.
checks.sequenceCheck: First node includes no collection measurement, drainage route or antibiotic endpoint. Those findings are revealed only in later updates.
checks.repairRecord: Replaced an abscess-diagnosis giveaway with a trajectory-and-target imaging task. Removed a sentence announcing the missing CT and supplied contrast-related context without a numeric cutoff.

distractorChecks.temptation: Attribute postoperative infection to the incision and choose the most accessible target.
distractorChecks.rankingRationale: A focused superficial study could assess a localized port-site collection. The represented fever and deep pelvic symptoms require examination of the intra-abdominal field.
distractorChecks.counterfactual: A focal swollen erythematous port-site mass with otherwise reassuring recovery could make a targeted superficial study appropriate.

distractorChecks.temptation: Treat the distension as a bowel-gas question while underweighting the inflammatory trajectory.
distractorChecks.rankingRationale: Radiographs can depict a bowel-gas pattern but provide limited characterization of an intra-abdominal infectious source. The renewed fever and deep pain make source mapping consequential.
distractorChecks.counterfactual: A distinct supported bowel-obstruction or foreign-body question could call for radiographs. The present source-control investigation has a different target.

checks.interpret: Integrate an organized gas-containing collection and persistent symptoms as incomplete source control, then assess localization and the actual catheter path.
checks.apply: Choose image-guided drainage for the accessible localized source while continuing shared antimicrobial care.
checks.closestError: Continue antibiotics because the patient is stable, or operate because postoperative gas is interpreted as proof of uncontrolled bowel leakage.
checks.decidingObservation: Persistent infection, a single organized collection with a bowel-free catheter route and no represented ongoing leak or generalized peritonitis.
checks.consequence: Delayed source control or an unnecessarily invasive operation.
checks.deletionTest: Deleting persistent symptoms makes continued medical care more plausible. Deleting route anatomy makes the drainage recommendation underspecified. Generalized-peritonitis and leak observations constrain the choice against operative source control. The 5.5-cm value is a constructed case observation and supplies no universal drainage cutoff.
checks.counterfactual: Add diffuse rigidity and active enteric leakage on CT. Operative exploration with control of the leak becomes the best offered source-control plan.
checks.cueAttack: All three options are concrete source-control policies. The key has intermediate length. The catheter path is necessary procedural anatomy, and is described without saying the procedure is available or will avoid delay. Every offered test/procedural choice has an explicit timing classification.
checks.stageCategory: Source-control route after cross-sectional anatomy and observed antibiotic response.
checks.difficulty: Predicted moderate to hard for PGY-2/3 from balancing persistent infection against stability, postoperative gas and actual source-control access.
checks.oneBestAnswer: For this localized accessible collection with persistent illness, catheter drainage is the favored proposed route. There is no claimed size-only rule or universal rank across all postoperative abscesses.
checks.sequenceCheck: The prior node explains source localization only. It supplies neither the drain route nor a general percutaneous-drainage recommendation. This update adds the decisive anatomy and response.
checks.repairRecord: Removed a sentence declaring the collection drainable and replaced it with the posterior path anatomy. Re-solved the operative-leak and resolving-collection counterfactuals.

distractorChecks.temptation: Treat stable physiology as evidence that antimicrobial treatment has controlled the source.
distractorChecks.rankingRationale: Antibiotics can suffice for selected small or resolving collections. Persistent infection with this organized accessible collection supports evacuation as part of source control.
distractorChecks.counterfactual: A small collection shrinking with complete clinical improvement and no safe access route could support continued medical management.

distractorChecks.temptation: Treat every postoperative gas-containing collection as a failure requiring a return to the operating room.
distractorChecks.rankingRationale: Exploration can control generalized contamination, an ongoing enteric leak or a collection inaccessible to percutaneous treatment. The supplied single localized collection has a safe catheter route and stable physiology.
distractorChecks.counterfactual: Diffuse rigidity and active enteric leakage would favor prompt operative source control.

checks.interpret: Separate a falling mildly abnormal leukocyte count from clinical evidence of persistent infection after adequate drainage.
checks.apply: End the completed active course instead of extending to a laboratory or radiographic endpoint.
checks.closestError: Continue antibiotics until the leukocyte count enters the laboratory reference interval.
checks.decidingObservation: Adequate source control, completed active treatment and afebrile pain-free functional recovery.
checks.deletionTest: Deleting source-control adequacy or clinical recovery invalidates the stop recommendation. The mildly abnormal falling count creates the closest competing endpoint. Four days is the constructed completed course with direct support from Global Alliance statement 8, not a newly authored mandatory minimum.
checks.counterfactual: Replace recovery with renewed deep pain and fever. Continuing active treatment while obtaining CT to assess a residual source becomes the best offered plan, with duration determined after reassessment.
checks.cueAttack: All labels specify antibiotic endpoints. The key and alternatives have comparable length. Every CT-containing plan has a CT estimate. No specific regimen is chosen because the active regimen is common background care. Removed a negative-culture result that would have provided an extra stopping cue.
checks.stageCategory: Antibiotic management after a completed active course and documented source control.
checks.difficulty: Predicted moderate for PGY-2/3 from treating incomplete laboratory normalization as treatment failure despite source control and recovery.
checks.oneBestAnswer: The represented completed-course scenario fits fixed short-course evidence. Minimum duration, resistant pathogens, immunosuppression and unresolved source-control scenarios require separate decisions.
checks.sequenceCheck: Prior feedback establishes the reason for drainage, while this node adds actual evacuation, clinical response and a completed antibiotic course. Earlier feedback states no antibiotic endpoint or duration.
checks.repairRecord: Replaced a duration-recall question with a source-control-and-recovery endpoint. Removed a new drug regimen and retained the observed completed course. The counterfactual was re-solved for recurrent illness.

distractorChecks.temptation: Use a mildly abnormal leukocyte count as proof of ongoing infection despite recovery.
distractorChecks.rankingRationale: Waiting for every inflammatory laboratory value to normalize can prolong therapy after adequate source control and clinical recovery. Fixed short-course evidence supports ending the completed course in this represented patient.
distractorChecks.counterfactual: Renewed fever, pain or organ dysfunction would require a fresh source-control assessment and a supported active-treatment plan.

distractorChecks.temptation: Require another source-imaging assessment despite documented source control and clinical recovery.
distractorChecks.rankingRationale: Clinical recovery after adequate drainage supports ending the completed course. New or persistent illness would establish a separate indication for CT assessment of residual infection while treatment is reassessed.
distractorChecks.counterfactual: Recurrent deep pain and fever would support CT assessment for a residual or new source while therapy is reassessed.
